results.explanation: The selected question is "Depression among adults" measured as crude prevalence (%) for the overall adult population in North Carolina and the United States from 2019 to 2023. The data include 10 matching records with no missing values or years. For North Carolina, the first recorded prevalence in 2019 was 21.6%, increasing to 23.1% in 2023, with the highest annual mean of 23.1% in 2023, showing an overall increase from first to last year. For the United States, the prevalence began at 18.8% in 2019, peaked at 20.6% in 2022, and slightly declined to 20.2% by 2023, indicating a net increase over time. In 2023, North Carolina’s prevalence (23.1%) was 3.0 percentage points higher than the national prevalence (20.2%). These indicators represent population-level estimates and do not provide information about any individual’s mental health status.

The selected question is "Depression among adults," measured as crude prevalence (%) for females in North Carolina from 2019 to 2023. There are 5 matching records, all with valid numeric values and no missing data. The first observed year, 2019, had a prevalence of 27.5%, and the latest year, 2023, had a prevalence of 28.0%, showing a slight increase over time. The highest annual mean was 28.7% in 2022. No years are missing for this location and demographic. These results represent population-level CDC indicators and do not provide individual mental health information.

The selected question is "Depression among adults" measured as crude prevalence percentage (%) for adult males in North Carolina and the United States from 2020 to 2022. There are six matching records, all with valid numeric values and no missing data. For North Carolina males, the first observed year 2020 had a prevalence of 15.2%, the highest annual mean was 16.3% in 2021, and the latest year 2022 recorded 14.1%, showing a slight decrease from 2021 to 2022. For U.S. males, the prevalence increased from 13.1% in 2020 to 14.9% in 2022, with 14.3% in 2021; the overall direction was upward. Comparing 2022 data, North Carolina males had a 14.1% prevalence versus 14.9% in the U.S., a difference of -0.8 percentage points. These indicators reflect population-level estimates and do not provide individual mental health information.

The selected question is "Depression among adults," with data measured as crude prevalence percentages for adults aged 18-44 in North Carolina from 2019 to 2021. There are 3 matching records, all with valid numeric data and no missing values, covering the years 2019, 2020, and 2021 continuously. The first observed year, 2019, has an annual mean prevalence of 22.6%; in 2020, it decreased to 21.3%; then in 2021, it increased to the highest annual mean of 24.5%. From 2019 to 2021, the crude prevalence first declined and then rose above the initial level by 1.9 percentage points. These are population-level CDC indicators and do not provide information about any individual's mental health.
